title: Michigan remote school sends holiday packages to students - NewsBreak
text:
By Zack Priehs ,
55 minutes ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — As the holiday quickly approaches, one local school is taking the opportunity to give its students an extra special Christmas.
The Insight School of Michigan is a remote alternative school with students all across Michigan, whose mission is to give those students a second chance at a high school education and a better life going forward. It serves students ages 16 to 22, and last year alone saw more than 300 students graduate.
(WLNS) Wednesday, they gave even more than education, busy packaging gifts for their students. This marks the school’s seventh annual Holiday of Hope, and this year, they’ll be sending 10 of their students gift packages, some of which might not otherwise receive gifts.
Mary Kimball, the school’s At-Risk Coordinator, said she’s happy to see kids having a special Christmas.
“I’m always impressed. It just warms my heart, I’m always impressed with how much comes in, with how much our staff are willing to give back, knowing that they have their own families, their own financial situations,” Kimball said.
(WLNS) For the Holiday of Hope, workers with the school say they “adopt” students, collect a list of wants and needs, and purchase gifts out of their own pockets.
“We started out with just a few. We didn’t know how well it would take off, and it’s really grown quite a bit. This is all volunteer by our staff,” Kimball said. “Our teachers and staff are all very generous and want to give back to our students in need.”
The packages contain things like winter coats, boots, and even diapers, are being shipped all over the state, including to some students right here in mid-Michigan, and are set to arrive by Christmas Day.
